edition.alertText: Democrats sweep US midterms — take House and Senate in blue wave driven by Iran war backlash; oil crashes 9% — Brent plunges to $94.62, biggest single-day drop since July; WTI falls to $86.97; Iran says Americans voted 'NO TO WAR'; Mojtaba Khamenei warns of 'immediate' response if Trump resumes post-midterm strikes; Trump says he'd 'do it again' and signals 'heavy hit'; Vance calls Iran war the 'obvious' reason for Republican rout; IRGC claims multiple tanker strikes — 'emboldened' after elections; Iranian general warns of Red Sea attacks if fighting resumes; Democrats demand end to war — plan to use new Congressional majority to curb war powers; tankers catch fire near Hormuz as IRGC claims mines; VLCC rates fall sharply on peace hopes; gold slips to $3,912; Qatar draft proposal still under review; Houthis claim missile attack on Saudi city; Saudi coalition strikes Hodeidah; ~2/3 of Americans disapprove of Trump's Iran war handling (Pew); war cost estimated at $2,000/household (Moody's); US gasoline at $4.13/gal (AAA)

situation: The Strait of Hormuz crisis reached day 250 as Democrats swept the US midterm elections, capturing both the House and Senate in a decisive rebuke of President Trump's handling of the Iran war. The blue wave sent shockwaves through energy markets and fundamentally altered the political calculus around the conflict. Vice President Vance called the Iran war the 'obvious' reason for the Republican rout, while Trump told reporters he'd 'do it again' and signaled a potential 'heavy hit' on Iran — a message at odds with the diplomatic track. Iran's Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf declared Americans had 'said NO TO WAR,' while Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned of an 'immediate' response if Trump resumes strikes in a post-midterm escalation — and insisted that US hostility toward Iran would persist regardless of which party controls Congress. Democrats wasted no time announcing plans to use their new majority to curb Trump's war powers, with incoming Speaker Jeffries and Senate Majority Leader Schumer signaling immediate action on a binding war powers resolution. An Iranian general warned of Red Sea attacks if fighting resumes, raising the specter of a wider maritime disruption beyond Hormuz. Qatar said both sides were still reviewing the draft peace proposal, with no breakthrough in sight despite the diplomatic momentum generated by the election results. The IRGC claimed it was 'emboldened' by the midterm outcome and struck multiple tankers transiting Hormuz 'without permission,' even as the diplomatic window remained nominally open.

Oil markets experienced their second major crash in a week as Brent crude plunged 8.9% to settle at $94.62 — the lowest since early August and down more than 19% from the October 30 peak of $117.64. WTI collapsed to $86.97 (-9.0%), falling below $90 for the first time since July. The sell-off was driven by traders pricing in a higher probability of a ceasefire deal under a Democratic Congress, with Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan both noting that war powers legislation could force Trump's hand. Gold slipped to $3,912/oz (-0.58%) as reduced safe-haven demand offset geopolitical uncertainty. Newcastle coal eased to $146.20/tonne (-2.21%) on expectations that a Hormuz reopening could restore LNG flows and reduce coal-for-gas substitution. US gasoline fell to $4.13/gal (AAA), down from $4.15 on the week. VLCC fixtures for Arabian Gulf routes dropped sharply on peace hopes — AG-China rates fell to an estimated $380K–420K/day range, down from $469K the previous session, though still well above the $200K market average. The Breakwave bi-weekly tanker report estimated Hormuz crude flows at approximately 11.7 million b/d in October. About 80 VLCCs remain in Gulf-of-Oman shuttle operations. Shipping and logistics costs continue to account for roughly 30% of per-barrel costs versus 5% pre-war (ADNOC). Cumulative global inventory drawdown since the start of the Hormuz disruption has reached approximately 1 billion barrels.

The maritime situation remained volatile despite the peace optimism. The IRGC claimed it was 'emboldened' after the midterm results and announced strikes on multiple tankers, claiming four vessels were 'destroyed' by mines while two more were 'detained' for transiting without permission — claims that CENTCOM has consistently called false. The Maritime Executive reported Iran was escalating maritime provocations precisely because the election results reduced the immediate threat of a post-midterm US military campaign. UKMTO continued to log attacks near Hormuz, with a vessel reported struck by unknown projectiles. The estimated wartime attack total now stands at approximately 207 incidents. On the Yemen front, the Houthis claimed a missile attack on a Saudi city after the kingdom struck targets in Hodeidah and Dhamar. Yemeni forces shelled Houthi-held areas with casualties reported. Houthi ground forces remain within 80 km of Aden. An estimated 350–400 ships remain stranded in the Arabian Gulf, with approximately 490 vessels waiting outside the strait. QatarEnergy's LNG force majeure remains in effect through the end of December 2026. Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz remain at zero for the fourth consecutive month. The FAO Food Price Index remains elevated. On the diplomatic track, the Qatar-mediated draft proposal is still under review by both sides, but the dramatic political shift in Washington has injected new uncertainty about whether Trump will pursue a deal or a post-election military campaign — a question that Iran, the Gulf states, and global markets are all watching closely.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices above $1,000/tonne — more than doubled since pre-war — feeding into phosphate production costs; Egypt, Brazil, India cutting output. Mosaic phosphate plants remain curtailed including South Fort Meade (Florida) — 199 workers laid off. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war. Phosphate prices up 25-30%. Trade routes shifting as Morocco and China seek alternative sources (ChemAnalyst).

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz at zero for fourth consecutive month — September, October, and early November all zero (World Visualized/Syz Group/Fertilizer Daily). Urea exports from Hormuz-dependent economies fell 83% YoY in April (ITC). ~850kt urea stranded. 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. Pakistan faces 200,000-ton fertiliser shortfall (Express Tribune). FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). World Bank: fertilizer prices surging as Hormuz disruptions tighten supplies. India building two fertiliser futures — diversifying sources while lobbying for corridor (Diplomat Magazine). Urea-to-corn ratio at 126 bushels/tonne vs 75 in Dec 2025 (CSIS). IFPRI: no bypass route for ammonia or sulfur unlike crude. UN fertilizer corridor stalled pending US-Iran agreement. Hormuz crude recovery hides slower one for LNG, fertilizer, helium and aluminum — non-oil flows still near zero (Enterprise AM).

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure through end of December 2026 — 8th consecutive extension since April. Global LNG supply gap estimated at ~600 bcf. Dutch TTF gas at €97.53/MWh (~$108.51), highest since 2022 energy crisis. Pakistan to pay >$1B for winter LNG spot cargoes at ~2x Qatari contract price. Qatari LNG carrier Al Mayeda struck near Hormuz (Oct 31). Bangladesh struggling with spot market costs. Lufthansa says 2026 fuel costs €2B higher amid Iran war. Europe and Asia face tight supply heading into winter. JERA CEO says Qatar LNG supply unlikely to recover soon.

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Methanol down 80% (ITC). Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint. ExxonMobil Q3 profit more than doubled to $15.4B on energy surge. Aramco Q3 profit surges 34.6% to $36.3B.
